Cross-Platform Builds > Cross-Compiling for ARM and macOS

Cross-Compiling for ARM and macOS

The ARM and macOS targets do not need a separately prepared toolchain: stock Zig 0.17.0 ships the required libc (musl/glibc/darwin), so you can cross-compile directly on a Linux x86_64 host. This differs from FreeBSD (see the FreeBSD Cross-Compilation page).

ARM Linux (aarch64)

# 运行目录：sci 仓库根目录
zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-linux-gnu -Dllvm=false -p zig-out-arm
file zig-out-arm/bin/sa
# 期望：ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64, ... interpreter /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1

macOS (ARM / Intel)

# 运行目录：sci 仓库根目录
zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-macos -Dllvm=false -p zig-out-mac-arm
zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-macos -Dllvm=false -p zig-out-mac-x64
file zig-out-mac-arm/bin/sa
# 期望：Mach-O 64-bit arm64 executable

Products include sa, hubproxy, libsa_asm.a, libsa_std.a, and libsa_std.dylib.

Known Fix: the recvmsg Symbol Name

portableRecvmsg in src/runtime/sa_std.zig once declared the libc function as extern "c" fn c_recvmsg — that symbol does not exist at all. Linux could link because ELF shared libraries allow undefined symbols, while a macOS dylib rejects them by default (undefined symbol: _c_recvmsg). It has been fixed to the real symbol name recvmsg. Lesson: when adding an extern declaration, the name must match the target libc's actual symbol character for character, and it should be verified on macOS (strict dylib linking).

NoteOn macOS, the recvmsg semantics, the __error() errno path, and the msghdr layout have not yet been test-run on real hardware; cross-compilation currently guarantees only that linking passes.
